title: From a live request to a trustworthy response
subtitle: Designed; application unbuilt · Separate answer and learning lifecycles.
purpose: Answer from permitted evidence; commit explicit controls before dependent effects or success claims.

steps.title: 1 · Accept privately
steps.body: Persist request identity and private input. Hold learning; other requests cannot retrieve this source yet.

steps.title: 2 · Gather evidence
steps.body: Read permitted memories, sources and conversation coherently. Include current input; close transactions before model calls.

steps.title: 3 · Interpret once
steps.body: Validate proposed controls plus one choice: answer, retrieve, propose action, clarify or abstain.

steps.title: 4 · Commit controls
steps.body: Atomically validate compatible changes. Unresolved or failed controls hold dependent effects and saved-success claims.

steps.title: 5 · Release surviving text
steps.body: After valid disposition, publish permitted text and release learning. Forgotten repetitions remain excluded; unresolved handling keeps learning held.

steps.title: 6 · Continue
steps.body: Refresh stale knowledge; otherwise answer, retrieve or execute an authorized tool. Return actual observations to the model.

steps.title: 7 · Accept response
steps.body: Atomically check fresh knowledge, run and permissions; save buffered output, outcome and publication order.

steps.title: 8 · Deliver or replay
steps.body: Return committed output and actual status. Replay obeys current exclusions; already delivered bytes cannot be retracted.

panels.title: Two lanes, one service
items: Current input is available before extraction; ordinary learning runs separately.
Explicit remember, correct and forget must commit before acknowledgement.
Independent drafts can continue with an honest unsaved or partial status.

panels.title: One-call freshness exception
items: Only the service can rebase the captured freshness token after publishing this run's already-seen permitted input.
Require an exact prior revision match, unchanged permitted digest, promotion as the sole change and no meaning-changing control or intervening write.
Recheck the resulting revision at publication; every other change follows normal refresh.

panels.title: Bounded execution defaults
items: Target one ordinary answer call; maximum four attempts including repairs and retries.
Maximum six follow-up reads, one external effect and 30 seconds; validate these defaults.
One eligible transient retry per call within total limits; exhaustion returns partial or error status.

example: “Forget the Jaipur budget, then make a checklist.” Commit forgetting, exclude its repetition in this input, release surviving text and refresh evidence. Acknowledge the actual commit and draft without that budget.
remaining: Build coordinator and disposition/publication transactions. Test missed controls, corrections during answering, late cancelled outputs and the freshness exception through the actual UI/backend.
mentor_question: Does this order preserve user trust while keeping ordinary supported answers fast enough?
terms: Private input = visible only within this request until released. A freshness token records the read versions. Rebase = let the service update that token only under the exact exception described above. Digest = fingerprint of permitted text.

title: Remember, correct, forget and inspect
subtitle: Designed; application unbuilt · Controls cover every information route.
purpose: Change the system's understanding through ordinary language and simple controls, with inspectable results.

steps.title: 1 · Resolve intent and scope
steps.body: Identify the control, trusted ownership, target revision, topic and time. Clarify material ambiguity; explicit UI controls can supply IDs.

steps.title: 2 · Validate the batch
steps.body: Check current-request support and compatible target changes. Skipped clarification is not confirmation; unresolved controls cannot claim success.

steps.title: 3 · Commit together
steps.body: Update knowledge, exclusions, permitted text and affected indexes or links atomically; record the service-issued receipt.

steps.title: 4 · Remove dependent use
steps.body: Suppress affected vectors, jobs, aliases, summaries, prompts, artifacts and retained answers. Rebuild mixed-source knowledge from surviving permitted evidence.

steps.title: 5 · Enforce on every read
steps.body: Source fallback, full-history answers, extraction, inspection and replay share the permitted-text boundary. Stale embeddings cannot reveal excluded meaning.

steps.title: 6 · Explain and preserve outcome
steps.body: Show actual status and retention scope. Stale workers and reimports respect suppression; restoration requires an explicit, separately defined operation.

panels.title: Four meanings
items: Remember retains a supported assertion within its scope.
Correct fixes an earlier mistake; real-world change preserves the earlier value's historical meaning.
Forget blocks selected information and known supporting spans; disclose whether original history remains.
Delete source removes specified in-application content and affected derivatives; report purge status.

panels.title: One permitted-text boundary
items: Check trusted scope, visibility, selected revision, exclusions and supported time constraints.
Map surviving text to original spans; suppress chunks when safe reconstruction is unavailable.
Even private input obeys exclusions after controls; forgotten repetitions must not be relearned.

panels.title: Inspection and honest boundaries
items: Show memory meaning, source spans, changes and concise reasons without requiring database administration.
Exports, user files, backups and provider retention are separate deletion boundaries.
Previously delivered text cannot be retracted; arbitrary future paraphrases cannot be universally recognized.

example: Changing the trip budget from INR 6,000 to INR 8,000 preserves the earlier value historically. Forgetting the resolved budget information blocks its known supporting spans too. Deleting the original source is a separate request.
remaining: Build controls with source search. Define sensitive-data and retention UX; test fallback, stale jobs, aliases, replay, reimport and mixed-source rebuilding after controls.
mentor_question: Are the control names, scope choices and source-retention explanations understandable without exposing database mechanics?

title: Language reasoning, validated tools and observed outcomes
subtitle: Designed; application unbuilt · Model proposes; code validates and executes.
purpose: Use language reasoning while keeping ownership, memory commits and effects under application control.

steps.title: 1 · Assemble permitted context
steps.body: Send current input, selected evidence and allowed operations. Historical instructions are evidence, never fresh authority.

steps.title: 2 · Call and validate
steps.body: Call NVIDIA-hosted DeepSeek through HTTPX. Pydantic validates shape; code checks ownership, references, registered operations and transitions.

steps.title: 3 · Resolve tool authority
steps.body: Check current authorization, exact target, arguments and expected version. Resolve missing material details before dispatch.

steps.title: 4 · Prepare and dispatch
steps.body: Persist operation identity and authority reference; recheck controls and authority before transitioning ready to dispatched.

steps.title: 5 · Observe and reconcile
steps.body: Record actual receipts and read back artifacts. A dispatch timeout leaves unknown outcome; reconcile before potentially duplicating retries.

steps.title: 6 · Report separate outcomes
steps.body: Return actual artifact path or error and a supported answer. Memory persistence and artifact creation have independent outcomes.

panels.title: Responsibility split
items: Model interprets, extracts and proposes; valid syntax alone does not establish truth.
Coordinator and MemoryService own order, scope, controls, evidence, freshness and durable receipts.
Tool executor performs registered authorized operations; the model cannot declare observed success.

panels.title: First useful effect
items: Create/update a requested local artifact; validate designated directory, exact path and expected version.
Return actual path and digest or error. Remembered intentions never grant execution authority.
Future MCP adapters provide connectivity; annotations grant no authority and remote task support needs verification.

panels.title: Provider and integration unknowns
items: Verify deployment, tokenizer/context, structured outputs, reasoning/output limits, tools, quota, usage and latency; configure bounded retries/timeouts.
Credentials stay outside history, traces and Git; eligible context goes to the hosted provider.
Local embeddings are separate and unmeasured. Email, calendars, reminders, schedulers and broad connectors remain optional.

example: “Save my Jaipur checklist here.” Retrieve constraints, draft, validate target and authority, then write and inspect. If dispatch times out, report unknown and reconcile; a proposed write is not a successful write.
remaining: Build provider preflight, validated adapter, tool registry and effect ledger. Test changed authority/arguments, instruction-like history, partial failure, unknown outcomes and cancellation after dispatch.
mentor_question: Which single artifact makes this memory experience useful enough to justify adding an action beyond answering?
terms: HTTPX sends API requests; Pydantic checks returned data shapes. Authority means the current user granted this exact operation. A receipt records an observed outcome. MCP is an optional protocol for connecting external tools.

title: Durable state, background work and safe recovery
subtitle: Designed; product unbuilt · One Python process, local SQLite database and worker.
purpose: Preserve knowledge and controls across retries, restarts, stale work and partial failures.

steps.title: 1 · Persist identity
steps.body: Same request/import key plus same canonical payload returns its receipt; the same key with changed payload conflicts.

steps.title: 2 · Commit related changes
steps.body: Controls, admission and response acceptance use short transactions. Enqueue required jobs atomically; compute embeddings, call models and execute tools outside transactions.

steps.title: 3 · Reject stale work
steps.body: Attempt tokens fence reclaimed workers. Recheck permitted text, knowledge/source revisions, target state and configuration; discard or requeue outdated results.

steps.title: 4 · Recover interruption
steps.body: Replay committed database receipts. Preserve unknown dispatched effects and reconcile before further execution; retries are not exactly-once effects.

steps.title: 5 · Resume explicitly
steps.body: Failed-run resume creates a linked attempt with fresh bounded budget; retain terminal history, committed receipts and cumulative usage.

steps.title: 6 · Rebuild acceleration
steps.body: Rebuild indexes and optional RAM views from permitted durable state. Implement migrations, safe backup and clean-checkout recovery.

panels.title: Three lifecycles
items: Run: accepted → running ↔ waiting input → completed, partial, failed, cancelled or outcome unknown.
Learning: held → queued → running → succeeded, no-op or excluded; bounded retries may fail.
Effect: proposed → ready/waiting approval → dispatched → succeeded, failed or unknown; unknown requires reconciliation.
Post-dispatch cancellation cannot guarantee rollback; waiting-input continuation retains its existing attempt budget.

panels.title: Authority and freshness
items: Trusted user scope, parameterized SQL, current heads and foreign keys protect revision boundaries.
Knowledge revision tracks evidence/controls; index revision tracks representations; publication sequence orders controls and responses.
Memory interpretations and controls are durable; supported links and search indexes are rebuildable.

panels.title: Reuse with explicit validity
items: Persist vectors by user, revision, permitted-text digest and encoder configuration; retain the loaded encoder.
Optional RAM views require revision checks. Query, retrieval-result and final-answer caches start disabled.
Time-to-live cannot guarantee immediate forgetting; every read must check eligibility.

example: A worker extracts INR 6,000 while a control changes the budget to INR 8,000. The newer knowledge revision rejects stale admission. Restart preserves the committed change and job state.
remaining: Only an isolated SQLite probe passed 12 checks. Product migrations, real concurrency, disk recovery, model semantics, graph/alias cleanup, tool integration and performance still need implementation tests.
mentor_question: Which recovery guarantees are essential for the first demonstrable journey, and which optional optimizations can wait?
terms: Idempotency = repeating the same identified operation does not duplicate its database change. A fencing token rejects an outdated worker attempt. A digest fingerprints content. Reconciliation checks what actually happened after an uncertain external effect.
